about: What each version changes for the people who use the board, newest first. The page shows the current version's items once per browser ("What's new") and the whole list behind "See all". Write for users, 3 to 5 short items per version, no internal names.

items: The Assignee menu lists people and lasting agents first; one-off runs are grouped under Others, and two actors with the same name show their id.
When you mention someone in a comment, the names that match come first and one-off runs last.
The unread counter counts open tickets only, so it goes back to zero.
On a phone: this note folds to one line, the Next view shows two-line titles and full ticket keys, and the view tabs fit.
A session is named after its first real line, not after a bracketed header a tool put above the prompt.
Important now means important to you: your priority, or the one you gave the ticket's project, places a ticket in the matrix.
A priority an agent set on your ticket reads P1? with who proposed it, and counts as P2 at most until you confirm it, unless there is a deadline.
Confirm a proposed priority in one click from the ticket, or by setting your own.
What your answer unblocks for the agents is still shown on the card, but no longer orders your lane or makes a ticket important.
An invited member who connects their own Claude Code now gets its questions, permission prompts and finished turns in their own "Waiting on you".
Those no longer land in the owner's lane.
Every person sees their own queue first: the first column is always "Waiting on you".
A ticket that waited a few times over its life can wait again: only the wakes of the last 7 days count toward the cap of 5.
When you lift a hold by hand, that count starts over (an agent lifting its own hold does not reset it).
A real loop between two tickets is still stopped, and goes to someone who decides.
A session opened from a ticket receives every new comment on it at its next turn: yours as your words, an agent's as information to check.
Only the ticket the session was opened on, never another one, and never an invited member's session.
ticket_get reminds agents to read a ticket in full when they take it up.
ticket_comment accepts body as well as text, like ticket_create.
A ticket_get that finds nothing says which board it read, so a missing server setting is easy to spot.
An empty ticket_list also names the board that answered.
Tag one Claude Code session from a ticket: mention it in a comment, and the comment reaches that session at its next turn.
The mention list offers the sessions seen in the last 30 minutes, with their repo, subject and start time.
Only your own comments can tag a session. (From 0.9.2, a session opened from a ticket also gets that ticket's other comments, as information to check.)
A link to a ticket (?ticket=ALV-12) opens that ticket again, open or closed.
The Done and On hold drawers are back under the lanes, with their counts.
If one part of the page fails to load, the rest still loads: the ticket you asked for and live updates included.
A ticket can now wait for a state of the world: "the motion sensor sees me come in", "the site answers again". Say it in words, with an optional deadline.
A watcher, a script or an agent lifts that wait with a proof in words as soon as it sees the state; the ticket comes back with the proof in its history.
When the deadline passes and nothing was seen, the ticket comes back by itself and says so, with its own next step if you gave one (for example: back to you).
OpenAI Codex CLI sessions can report to the board too: run the Codex setup script once (see the README), then trust the hooks in Codex.
A Codex session gets its own ticket with its repository and branch: in progress while it works, ready for review when a turn ends, done when it closes.
Codex can use every ticket tool (create, update, next, list, comment, get, hold, feedback); what it creates and changes shows as Codex.
Agents can now assign a ticket to themselves with "me", whichever agent they are.
Searching the board now finds projects too: the ones that match appear in a Projects group above the columns.
Typing a ticket key (ALV-12) always finds it, even for a project or an old closed ticket.
Without a search, nothing changes: projects stay in the Projects view.
On hold: a ticket that waits for something leaves every lane and comes back by itself when it happens. Open a ticket and use Put on hold.
It can wait for other tickets to close, a pull request to be merged, a date, or a reply from someone.
Then it wakes the agent that put it on hold (to check the work still makes sense), hands it to someone, or comes back to you.
Tickets on hold sit in their own drawer under the board, with what each one waits for; one that can no longer come back is marked stuck.
Every view now says when its data was last confirmed: "updated just now", "updated 3 min ago". Hover it for the exact time.
When the board cannot reach the server for a while, that line turns amber and says the view may be out of date.
An open ticket shows when it was loaded, at the top of its panel.
The short date beside a ticket is now its last change (comment, status, assignee), on the board, list and Next. Hover it for the creation date.
The Done button on your questions is slimmer: a hairline frame and the height of the other small buttons, still easy to hit on a phone.
Done in the ticket panel got the same lighter frame.
Attach any file, not only pictures: PDFs, text, archives, audio, video. Use the paperclip next to the text box, drop files on it, or paste a screenshot.
It works in a new ticket too, before you create it.
Before sending, each file shows as a chip with its name and size; × removes it. Files are capped at 25 MB each, or what the installation sets.
In the history a picture shows as a thumbnail, a PDF opens in the browser, any other file downloads with its own name.
Projects, next to Matrix (or press p): each long-running project with its latest state, its tickets and jobs, and what it waits on from you.
Projects no longer crowd To do and In progress: they stay open, on the Projects page.
A project is a ticket with the label front, and a ticket joins it as a sub-ticket or with the label front-id:<name> when the project carries it too.
An installation can pick another label, or turn projects off.
The server tells whoever runs it when a feature needs a setting that was never set: a warning when it starts, and the list in the version it reports.
A new feature that needs a setting now ships with a line saying so, and what stays off without it.
Nothing changes for an installation that has them all.
You can attach pictures to a comment: paste one or use Add picture (PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 8 MB). Click a thumbnail for full size.
Reply: a dot on a card when someone answered you since you last opened it. The counter in the bar shows only those (or press u).
Opening a ticket marks its replies read, on the server: read on your phone, read on your computer.
Your comment hands the ticket to the actor you mention, else to the router of the installation. It leaves your pile until they give it back.
Mentions now offer sub-actors too, found by their name.
Matrix, next to Board, Next and List (or press m): your tickets on an important × urgent grid, in four boxes from Do now to Later.
Urgent: a deadline within 2 days, or waiting on you 3 days. Important: P0 or P1, a top-half ⚡ ROI, or an answer that unblocks work.
A deadline is read from a due:YYYY-MM-DD label, or from the date in the "Without an answer" line of a request.
Mine shows what is assigned to you or waiting on you; All open shows every open ticket. Click a ticket to open it on the right.
A grip on the left edge of an open ticket: drag it to widen the ticket, double-click it to reset.
Copy and read wide are always visible on descriptions and comments, and work with a tap.
On a phone or in a narrow window, the button next to Done reads the whole ticket, comments included.
This note shows once after each update. See all changes opens the full history.
The ? button in the header lists every shortcut and gesture.
The Waiting on you lane can show a score per ticket (⚡ ROI), posted by your installation, with its reason on hover.
Scored tickets come first in the lane, highest first, and a line under the lane title says what waits on you.
An open ticket keeps its scroll position when it updates, and lands on your comment after you post it.
Agents can read a ticket in full, every comment complete.
Ticket actions: buttons your installation declares appear in the open ticket, for example to start a job or open a related page.
A click runs the action on the server and can open a link or show a message in the ticket.
Only owners and admins see and run them, and every run is kept in the audit log.
Make the open ticket wider by dragging its left edge; the width is kept in this browser.
The expand button next to Done opens the ticket nearly full screen, its text in a readable column. Esc goes back.
Copy a description or a comment as markdown, or read it alone in a large reading view.
Long texts are never cut any more: up to 64 000 characters per comment or description, with a counter near the limit.
Nested lists and numbered lists render correctly in descriptions and comments.
